newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New HK rail link won't be held up, says train boss.
newsitem.headline: New HK rail link won't be held up, says train boss.

text.p: Hong Kong's railway chief said on Friday he was optimistic a proposed train link with China would not be delayed by squabbles between China and Britain as had happened to a new container port.
Hong Kong will revert to China next July 1, ending 150 years of colonial rule. Major infrastructure projects now effectively require Beijing's blessing.

China has criticised the handling of the Western Corridor Railway (WCR) project that would link Hong Kong's Kowloon Peninsula and western New Territories with China. Beijing has said the estimated HK$75 billion project is too expensive and voiced fears it would drain Hong Kong's treasury coffers.
"I don't believe (the WCR will become another Container Terminal 9)," Kevin Hyde, Kowloon-Canton Railway Corporation (KCRC) chairman and chief executive, told a news conference.
The CT9 container port project has been stalled since 1992 by China, which has not given its blessing to the developers who were awarded the contract by the Hong Kong government.
Chinese and British diplomats are still haggling over the railway, and the date for construction is nowhere in sight.
"I detect a very significant support for the line in China and clearly, there is tremendous support in Hong Kong," he said.

"China has just built a 2,500-km (1,550-mile) railway from Beijing to the (Hong Kong) border called the Beijing-Kowloon line, so I just conceive the WCR being the last 35 km (22 miles) of it," he said.

Hyde said he believed the project would be a priority for the Hong Kong and Chinese governments, and added that officials from both sides were talking about the compatibility of railway systems for the link.
Hyde, who retires by the end of this year, also said the KCRC would not withdraw more than HK$110 million untendered contracts to consultancy firms regarding feasibility studies on the WCR.
The 51 contracts awarded to 22 firms were carried out properly following the KCRC procedures, he said, rejecting criticism from China.
China has criticised the KCRC for handing out contracts for the railway without consulting Beijing.
